Maintenance Report — MNT-0176-003

Asset: WELL-0176 (NE-08 Well 176, T350, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: flowline Work started: 03 Mar 2023 08:00 · Finished: 04 Mar 2023 10:00 · Well stopped for this job: 26 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0176-0020 on 2023-03-02 Report written: 05 Mar 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0176-0020 at 14:00 on 2023-03-02 found crude oil on the pad: about 9.0% of the pad area, estimated 5.2 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.8 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

Root cause

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Cleaned free oil out of the cellar.
  2. Unbolted the flange and removed the failed gasket.
  3. Fitted a new gasket and new bolts, torqued to specification.
  4. Excavated the stained soil around the cellar.

Summary of the fix: replaced the flange gasket and bolts and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 369 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 295 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 3.1 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0176-003 (WS-06).
  • 4 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.2% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0176-005

Asset: WELL-0176 (NE-08 Well 176, T350, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 09 Jun 2023 08:00 · Finished: 04 Jul 2023 13:00 · Well stopped for this job: 605 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Megan Ward, Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0176-0034 on 2023-06-08 Report written: 04 Jul 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running rough with a loud knock at the top of each stroke, so the operator stopped it. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0176-0034 showed the wellhead at 35.1 °C with the air at 32.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 23 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

Grease contaminated with sand had worn the bearing.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 5 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

Bolts, shims and seals465
Bearing grease and consumables775

Total4,671

Notes and recommendations

  • Shorten the grease interval on this unit to 60 days.
  • Check saddle bearings on neighbouring units of the same age.
